decision: Retain macFUSE FSKit chunked scheme as candidate; reassess original VM+NFS architecture without new phone tests
native_fskit: comparison retained, blocked by Personal Team FSKit capability

confirmed_code_findings.finding: MtpWriteback::publish holds namespaceLock through snapshot->sync, including the whole remote upload and publication
readAt holds per-file recursive mutex across fetchRange; attributes acquires the same mutex
relocate and beginRemoval synchronously materialize retained file contents

evidence: Prior NFS RPCs blocked 20-31 seconds; synthetic delayed operations returned JUKEBOX but macOS still flagged not responding. Recent macFUSE combined tests also blocked before chunking, while chunking reduced waits. Thus frontend replacement alone is not established as necessary.
proposed_direction: Separate local namespace and durable state from protocol execution
Run one MTP owner with short transactions and explicit scheduling, first on known supported Samsung
Do not hold namespace/file-metadata locks over USB waits; pin immutable versions and reconcile publication by generation
Implement open-handle delete/rename semantics via deferred remote cleanup and stable logical identity, rather than mandatory synchronous materialization
Acknowledge NFS stable writes only after durable local data plus replayable metadata; remote-sync completion remains separate
Handle unsupported capabilities, device stalls and USB forwarding overhead explicitly
limitations: No VM/NFS integration test of chunked scheduler yet
Cannot guarantee silent responsiveness during arbitrary device stalls or missing uncached data
Not changing production code or NFS timeout defaults in this review
